newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Dole campaign finance violations alleged.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Dole campaign finance violations alleged.

text.p: A citizens' lobbying group called on Wednesday for the appointment of an independent counsel to investigate alleged "willful violations" of finance laws by the Democratic and Republican presidential campaigns.
The group, Common Cause, said "the violations that occurred during the 1996 presidential election are the most massive violations of the campaign finance laws since the Watergate scandal."

Common Cause alleged that President Bill Clinton's primary committee, working through the Democratic National Committee, and Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, working through the Republican National Committee, "engaged in an illegal scheme to circumvent the federal campaign finance laws."

It also alleged that both Clinton and Dole agreed during their primary election campaigns to comply with a spending limit of $37 million, compliance that was required in order for both candidates to receive federal matching funds.

However, the group alleged that both the Dole and Clinton campaigns spent tens of millions of dollars over the limit on television advertisements. Under U.S. election law, such spending is allowed only if the ads push a political party's ideas or issues, but not if they plainly support one candidate.

"These ads were Clinton and Dole candidate ads, plain and simple, and as candidate ads were subject to the contribution and spending limits that apply to presidential campaigns," Common Cause president Ann McBride told a news conference.
